requirements.requirement: Configure PostgreSQL streaming replication across node1, node2, node3 with node1 as the writable primary
requirements.summary: PostgreSQL 16 installed on all three nodes. node1 initialized as primary (wal_level=replica, replication slots node2_slot/node3_slot created, replicator role created). node2 and node3 were provisioned via pg_basebackup -R from node1 and started as standbys (pg_is_in_recovery=t). Live replication verified: an INSERT on node1 (appdb.demo) appeared on both standbys, and pg_stat_replication showed both in 'streaming'/'async' state with active slots.

requirements.requirement: Carry replication traffic over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A self-signed CA (CN=postgres-cluster-ca) was generated on node1 with openssl; per-node server certs (CN+SAN for node1/2/3) and a client cert (CN=replicator) were issued from that CA and distributed to all nodes. postgresql.conf on all nodes sets ssl=on with ssl_cert_file/ssl_key_file/ssl_ca_file pointing at the CA-issued material. pg_stat_ssl on the primary directly shows ssl=t and client_dn=/CN=replicator for both standby connections, both before and after a later restart, confirming TLS is actually in use for the replication streams, not just configured.

requirements.requirement: Accept replication connections only from peers presenting a certificate issued by that CA
requirements.summary: pg_hba.conf on node1 restricts replication to hostssl+cert auth from node2/node3 IPs only, with catch-all reject rules for other replication attempts. Falsification testing directly demonstrated the control: a non-SSL replication attempt was rejected ('no encryption'), an SSL attempt without a client cert was rejected ('connection requires a valid client certificate'), a cert signed by a freshly generated rogue CA was rejected ('SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca'), while a pg_basebackup using the CA-issued replicator cert succeeded (exit=0, backup completed). This is direct behavioral evidence, not just configuration.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, behavioral evidence: streaming replication from node1 (writable primary) to node2/node3 (standbys) is established and shown working via live data propagation; replication traffic is TLS-encrypted using a cluster-generated CA, confirmed by pg_stat_ssl showing ssl=t and the correct client_dn; and access is restricted to CA-issued certificates, proven by falsification tests that reject no-SSL, no-client-cert, and rogue-CA connections while accepting the CA-signed client cert. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also executed on all three nodes with pre-restart boot IDs, reboot acknowledgements, changed post-restart boot IDs (cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor snapshots, which match exactly), and full recovery of PostgreSQL, replication, TLS client-cert identity, and data on every node — this is not a task requirement but its presence and quality raise overall confidence rather than detract from it. The main blemish is CA/server/client private key material left behind in /tmp on all three nodes rather than being cleaned up post-deployment.
limitations: Restart/reboot recovery is not part of the public task contract, so it was evaluated only as supplemental cross-check evidence, not as a scored requirement; nonetheless all three nodes showed a coherent pre-restart baseline, changed boot identity, and full service/replication/data recovery, consistent with the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots.
CA and per-node/client private keys remain present under /tmp on all three nodes in the final captured state; while permissioned 600 and root-owned, this is retained residue that was not cleaned up.
Evidence is drawn from a single executor attempt's command trace and fixed lifecycle snapshots; no independent verification outside the provided evidence was possible.

operational_hygiene.summary: Overall hygiene is good: no failed services, no damaged package state, and firewall/config changes are all directly tied to the task. Two categories of minor unnecessary residue remain uncleaned on all three nodes after task completion: (1) the CA private key (/tmp/pgca/ca.key) and all per-node CSR/key material generated on node1 during certificate issuance were never removed from /tmp, and the copied server/client private keys distributed to node2 and node3 (/tmp/node2.key, /tmp/node3.key, /tmp/replicator.key, /tmp/ca.crt) also remain in /tmp per the after-executor snapshot, rather than being cleaned up once copied into PGDATA — a retained (not reverted) piece of security-sensitive residue, though mitigated by root-only 600 permissions. (2) Several troubleshooting/falsification artifacts (rogue CA key/cert, test pg_basebackup directories under /tmp) were properly created and then removed in the same command, so these were bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted. No unnecessary mutations were found that were broad, destructive, or that weakened access controls; the pg_hba.conf.orig backup and firewalld port openings are legitimate prerequisites/config for the task.
